frames.label: A $12k budget is sufficient to build a good-quality CNC router equipped with ballscrews and precision linear guides
frames.main_point: A $12k budget is sufficient to build a good-quality CNC router equipped with ballscrews and precision linear guides. Building rather than buying can meet capability targets within this cost.
frames.source_quote: with 12k$ budged you can build good quality router with ballscrews and precise linear guides.
frames.subject: DIY CNC router budget (ballscrews + linear guides)
frames.thread_title: Advice on precision CNC milling machines for PCB prototyping

frames.label: When submitting PCB jobs to Advanced Circuits, run their FreeDFM check as a standard step to validate your output fil...
frames.main_point: When submitting PCB jobs to Advanced Circuits, run their FreeDFM check as a standard step to validate your output files before ordering.
frames.source_quote: I've made several successful orders from Advanced Circuits and always check FreeDFM.
frames.subject: pre-order DFM check with Advanced Circuits FreeDFM
frames.thread_title: How do I get an Excellon Drill file with 2.4 precision and trailing zero suppression out of EAGLE?

frames.label: For non-exotic, small-run jobs at large firms, quotes are driven more by overhead and the client relationship than by...
frames.main_point: For non-exotic, small-run jobs at large firms, quotes are driven more by overhead and the client relationship than by detailed design complexity. The business context can outweigh feature-level analysis in determining price.
frames.source_quote: Firstly, if you're talking about small runs at a large company and the design doesn't include anything exotic, the pricing will probably have less to do with the specifics of your design, and more to do with the overhead costs and benefits of dealing with you as a client.
frames.subject: pricing drivers for small-run work at large companies
frames.thread_title: Understanding metalwork manufacture -- How are Purchase Quotations prepared?

frames.label: The evaluation is usually done very quickly by a senior person who understands the client relationship and the compan...
frames.main_point: The evaluation is usually done very quickly by a senior person who understands the client relationship and the company’s overall workload.
frames.source_quote: This evaluation is usually done very quickly by someone senior enough to understand the business relationship with the particular client and the overall workload of the company.
frames.subject: bid/no-bid gatekeeping for small projects
frames.thread_title: Understanding metalwork manufacture -- How are Purchase Quotations prepared?

frames.label: Fabrication labor estimates are developed with shop-floor personnel, covering setup, production, and inspection time...
frames.main_point: Fabrication labor estimates are developed with shop-floor personnel, covering setup, production, and inspection time for the entire run. Practitioner input grounds the time estimate in actual process reality.
frames.source_quote: For fabrication labor they would discuss the project with the folks who run the shop floor and estimate what time it would take to set up tooling, produce, and inspect the whole run.
frames.subject: shop-floor input to estimate fabrication labor
frames.thread_title: Understanding metalwork manufacture -- How are Purchase Quotations prepared?

frames.label: Quotes include time for management/overhead tasks such as material buying, submittal drawings, first articles, functi...
frames.main_point: Quotes include time for management/overhead tasks such as material buying, submittal drawings, first articles, functional testing, and shipping. These support activities are explicitly estimated as part of cost.
frames.source_quote: For management labor, they would estimate the amount of time to support the project, This would include things like material procurement, submittal drawings, first article production, functional tests, shipping, etc.
frames.subject: management/overhead tasks included in quotes
frames.thread_title: Understanding metalwork manufacture -- How are Purchase Quotations prepared?

frames.label: For the go/no-go triage, minimal information (e.g., a single image and brief description in proper industry terms) is...
frames.main_point: For the go/no-go triage, minimal information (e.g., a single image and brief description in proper industry terms) is sufficient. Full CAD packages aren’t required to decide whether to quote.
frames.source_quote: They need very few details about the actual design, often one image and a brief description would be enough if the client is familiar with the jargon of the industry and thus able to explain the task.
frames.subject: information sufficiency for quote triage
frames.thread_title: Understanding metalwork manufacture -- How are Purchase Quotations prepared?

frames.label: Shops may pursue low-margin jobs during slack periods to keep people and machines busy and avoid layoffs
frames.main_point: Shops may pursue low-margin jobs during slack periods to keep people and machines busy and avoid layoffs. Capacity risk can justify bidding work that would otherwise be declined on profitability grounds.
frames.source_quote: Similarly, even if it's a kind of work where the company has to give up most of its profits to be competitive, they may still decide to bid on the work if they are very low on work and at risk of having to lay off workers.
frames.subject: accepting low-margin work to maintain utilization
frames.thread_title: Understanding metalwork manufacture -- How are Purchase Quotations prepared?

frames.label: For small jobs, rely more on judgment than detailed estimating, because occasional small errors are tolerable while e...
frames.main_point: For small jobs, rely more on judgment than detailed estimating, because occasional small errors are tolerable while excessive bid-prep time can sink margin or make the quote uncompetitive. Limit analysis to what materially affects the price.
frames.source_quote: For smaller projects, lots more can and should be eyeballed. The reason for this is that a small loss (say 10% on a small project represents an amount of money that the company can probably tolerate losing occasionally when there's a mistake. Conversely, a few too many hours of manager or engineer time in the bidding process can quickly become a big enough cost as a percentage of the contract sum that either the company still loses money on it, or their bid is non-competitive.
frames.subject: eyeballing vs. detailed estimating on small projects
frames.thread_title: Understanding metalwork manufacture -- How are Purchase Quotations prepared?

frames.label: Use outcomes from similar past jobs to anchor a new quote, scaling for quantity and complexity
frames.main_point: Use outcomes from similar past jobs to anchor a new quote, scaling for quantity and complexity. Historical profit/loss provides a data-backed baseline that reduces the need for fresh detailed analysis.
frames.source_quote: Have we done a very similar project in the past? If so, often reviewing that project and the actual profit or loss can form a solid basis to bid the new work scaled by quantity and complexity.
frames.subject: analogous estimating from past projects
frames.thread_title: Understanding metalwork manufacture -- How are Purchase Quotations prepared?

frames.label: When the buyer’s budget expectation is well above true costs, a shop can choose a safe price without further estimati...
frames.main_point: When the buyer’s budget expectation is well above true costs, a shop can choose a safe price without further estimating effort. Known client anchors can reduce bid-preparation time on small jobs.
frames.source_quote: Do I know what the client is expecting this to cost? If the expectation is comfortably more than actual costs then they can pick a 'safe' number without doing any more work.
frames.subject: using client price expectations in quoting
frames.thread_title: Understanding metalwork manufacture -- How are Purchase Quotations prepared?

frames.label: Identify which cost categories dominate and estimate those in detail, applying percentage adders to minor categories
frames.main_point: Identify which cost categories dominate and estimate those in detail, applying percentage adders to minor categories. This prioritizes estimating effort where it moves the price most.
frames.source_quote: Are the materials, manufacturing labor, tooling, or management labor are obviously the majority of the costs? If it's clear that one or more of these cost categories was pretty small then they can focus efforts on pricing the ones that matter more and just apply a percentage to cover the others.
frames.subject: focus estimating on dominant cost drivers
frames.thread_title: Understanding metalwork manufacture -- How are Purchase Quotations prepared?

frames.label: For small runs, it’s often better to use in-stock common materials even with lower yield to avoid the cost and delay...
frames.main_point: For small runs, it’s often better to use in-stock common materials even with lower yield to avoid the cost and delay of ordering special stock. Waste can be cheaper than procurement overhead at small scale.
frames.source_quote: For materials, they would start by checking if the project can be done from a  material they ordinarily stock. Even if the yield isn't great, for a small run using common materials the waste will probably be worth the reduced cost of not having to order and receive another stock size.
frames.subject: using in-stock common materials for small runs despite poor yield
frames.thread_title: Understanding metalwork manufacture -- How are Purchase Quotations prepared?

frames.label: When planning tooling, first try to reuse or adapt existing tools, then look for off-the-shelf options, and only then...
frames.main_point: When planning tooling, first try to reuse or adapt existing tools, then look for off-the-shelf options, and only then plan custom tooling with engineering input. This minimizes lead time and nonrecurring cost.
frames.source_quote: They would start by seeing if any existing tooling can be used or adapted for the project. If not, they would check if there's a tool that can be purchased that accommodates the design. If not, then they would start the process with an engineer or determining what custom tooling (dies, stamps, workholding, etc) would be required and what the design and production effort would take.
frames.subject: tooling selection escalation (reuse → buy → custom)
frames.thread_title: Understanding metalwork manufacture -- How are Purchase Quotations prepared?

frames.label: If a required standard grade/condition of stock is readily available, machining directly from that stock is often the...
frames.main_point: If a required standard grade/condition of stock is readily available, machining directly from that stock is often the best way to minimize lead time.
frames.source_quote: When a normalized evaluation of a metal compound is mentioned that is promptly accessible, the CNC specialist co-op will machine the parts straightforwardly from that stock material. This is regularly the most ideal choice for decreasing lead times.
frames.subject: using readily available stock condition to reduce lead time
frames.thread_title: Is CNC milling on metals always followed by heat treatment?

frames.label: Design optimization should integrate feedback from manufacturing to avoid unnecessary costs such as longer runtime, m...
frames.main_point: Design optimization should integrate feedback from manufacturing to avoid unnecessary costs such as longer runtime, material waste, and accelerated tool wear. Considering process realities early leads to parts that are cheaper to produce.
frames.source_quote: But I think more generally -- design optimization should include feedback from the manufacturing process so that a useful part can be produced without extra costs - costs including runtime, material waste, tool wear, etc.
frames.subject: manufacturing feedback in design optimization
frames.thread_title: What is a purpose of learning G-code?

frames.label: CNC-machining these molds is inexpensive if the shop already owns a capable CNC mill
frames.main_point: CNC-machining these molds is inexpensive if the shop already owns a capable CNC mill. A basic non-junk CNC can be purchased for a few thousand dollars, which is small relative to commercial machining rates in the hundreds of dollars per hour, keeping per-part costs low.
frames.source_quote: That isn't an expensive process, so long as you have the CNC machine. A basic one that isn't junk for sale on E-bay would cost a few thousand dollars, which isn't a big deal for a commercial company if their selling price amounts to hundreds of dollars per hour of machining time.
frames.subject: CNC machining cost drivers: machine ownership vs billable rate
frames.thread_title: Low cost molds. Can such molds be produced?

frames.label: When moving from single prototypes to small-batch production, prioritize improving manufacturability and ensuring the...
frames.main_point: When moving from single prototypes to small-batch production, prioritize improving manufacturability and ensuring the design scales without special effort. Make design changes that reduce production friction and support repeatability.
frames.source_quote: I believe your primary goal when transitioning from single prototypes to small batch production should be to improve manufacturability, and ensure that your design is scalable.
frames.subject: transition to small-batch production priorities
frames.thread_title: From advanced prototype to low-volume production

frames.label: Before low-volume production, audit and redesign elements that won’t scale: ad‑hoc or undocumented builds, components...
frames.main_point: Before low-volume production, audit and redesign elements that won’t scale: ad‑hoc or undocumented builds, components hard to source in quantity, parts with known issues tolerated in a one‑off, labor‑intensive systems, and items that don’t meet aesthetic expectations.
frames.source_quote:
Examples of parts/systems that may need to be revised:

- Parts that were made without drawings, for example by match drilling, or "freestyling"
- Parts that are not easily obtainable in quantity
- Parts/systems that have known issues, which were manageable for a single prototype.
- Systems that require excessive manual labor for manufacture. For example hand soldered cable harnesses may need to be replaced with off-the-shelf options.
- Parts that are functional, but not aesthetically pleasing may need to be replaced
frames.subject: prototype part revision candidates for low-volume production
frames.thread_title: From advanced prototype to low-volume production

frames.label: Adopt a results-first mindset: simulate building 20 units now and identify the manufacturability, sourcing, and assem...
frames.main_point: Adopt a results-first mindset: simulate building 20 units now and identify the manufacturability, sourcing, and assembly problems that would occur, rather than focusing on specific methods.
frames.source_quote: I would recommend focusing less on methods, and more on results. Instead of asking "how do I level up", I would ask: "if I started making 20 of these right now, what problems would I run into".
frames.subject: production-readiness mindset for small batches
frames.thread_title: From advanced prototype to low-volume production

frames.label: For runs of roughly 10–20 units, alternatives to 3D printing generally cost more, so switching processes should be ju...
frames.main_point: For runs of roughly 10–20 units, alternatives to 3D printing generally cost more, so switching processes should be justified by clear benefits.
frames.source_quote: There are other options, but they will all be more expensive than 3D printing (for 10-20 units) so you will probably want to have a good reason for choosing something else.
frames.subject: cost of alternatives vs 3D printing at low volumes
frames.thread_title: From advanced prototype to low-volume production

frames.label: Small DIY/desktop CNC machines typically require many hours of tuning, may never achieve acceptable quality, and even...
frames.main_point: Small DIY/desktop CNC machines typically require many hours of tuning, may never achieve acceptable quality, and even when they do, they cut slowly. They are a poor choice for producing a short pilot run compared to outsourcing.
frames.source_quote: Those are cool and fun, but you will have to dick around with it for dozens of hours, and it may never produce good results, and if it does, it will be slow.
frames.subject: small DIY/desktop CNC suitability for production
frames.thread_title: Small scale manufacturing

frames.label: A $25-per-set quote is considered inexpensive for custom machined parts at low volumes
frames.main_point: A $25-per-set quote is considered inexpensive for custom machined parts at low volumes. This indicates that outsourcing the pilot batch can be cost-effective.
frames.source_quote: 25 bucks a set for parts is actually quite cheap for custom machined stuff.
frames.subject: low-volume custom machining cost benchmark
frames.thread_title: Small scale manufacturing

frames.label: When per-unit machining quotes are low, paying a few thousand dollars for a limited run is a straightforward way to v...
frames.main_point: When per-unit machining quotes are low, paying a few thousand dollars for a limited run is a straightforward way to validate a product. Unless budget is extremely tight, outsourcing the pilot batch is likely the best option.
frames.source_quote: You could just bite the bullet and spend $2500 bucks to test the idea. That's simple and straight forward and unless you're on a shoe-string budget probably the best option.
frames.subject: outsourcing pilot run vs DIY investment
frames.thread_title: Small scale manufacturing

frames.label: Use a hybrid approach by combining manufacturing methods to balance cost, strength, and appearance
frames.main_point: Use a hybrid approach by combining manufacturing methods to balance cost, strength, and appearance. Assign each part to the process that best suits its requirements.
frames.source_quote: The best bet is probably to combine these methods as necessary.
frames.subject: hybrid prototyping process selection
frames.thread_title: Small scale manufacturing

frames.label: Design parts so they require as few manufacturing operations as possible; minimizing steps improves manufacturability...
frames.main_point: Design parts so they require as few manufacturing operations as possible; minimizing steps improves manufacturability by reducing handling, setups, and complexity.
frames.source_quote: Ideally, a part should have as little steps to produce as possible
frames.subject: operation count minimization
frames.thread_title: Small scale manufacturing

frames.label: During design, mentally simulate the manufacturing process: consider toolpaths, cut direction, workholding, fixtures/...
frames.main_point: During design, mentally simulate the manufacturing process: consider toolpaths, cut direction, workholding, fixtures/jigs, assembly, and mold-related needs like pull direction, draft, and minimum radii to ensure the part is manufacturable.
frames.source_quote: When designing a part I always imagen that I am the machine that has to manufacture it, you have to imagen the tool paths, cut direction, how you're going to hold it, fixtures, jigs, assembly, and if applicable things like pull direction, drafts, minimum radii etc.
frames.subject: DFM mental simulation of manufacturing
frames.thread_title: Small scale manufacturing

frames.label: Do not default to CNC machining as the only solution; evaluate alternative processes like casting, injection molding,...
frames.main_point: Do not default to CNC machining as the only solution; evaluate alternative processes like casting, injection molding, laser/waterjet cutting, EDM, or 3D printing based on the part’s needs.
frames.source_quote: CNC machining isn't a silver bullet either, you have casting, injection moulding, laser, waterjet, EDM and of course 3D printing.
frames.subject: process selection beyond CNC machining
frames.thread_title: Small scale manufacturing

frames.label: For short-run production, the total cost of buying, setting up, and learning a small CNC often ends up at least 2–3×...
frames.main_point: For short-run production, the total cost of buying, setting up, and learning a small CNC often ends up at least 2–3× higher once you include labor time and schedule delays. This makes DIY machining uneconomical compared to external sourcing for limited batches.
frames.source_quote: The cost of buying, setting up, learning how to properly use a small cnc machine will be at least 2 or 3 times greater if you factor in work hours, and delays.
frames.subject: in-house small CNC investment for short-run production
frames.thread_title: Small scale manufacturing

frames.label: Investing in DIY manufacturing equipment only starts to make economic sense when you plan to scale to the order of th...
frames.main_point: Investing in DIY manufacturing equipment only starts to make economic sense when you plan to scale to the order of thousands of pieces. Below that volume, the payback is unlikely to justify the upfront cost and learning curve.
frames.source_quote: A final thought, is that an investment on DIY equipment would make sense, if you are planning to scale production to probably something in the order of a few thousand pieces.
frames.subject: DIY equipment investment break-even volume
frames.thread_title: Small scale manufacturing

frames.label: Redesign parts to suit more cost-effective manufacturing methods while preserving function
frames.main_point: Redesign parts to suit more cost-effective manufacturing methods while preserving function. DFM-driven changes can significantly reduce production cost without sacrificing performance.
frames.source_quote: it would probably make more sense to adjust design in order to accommodate for more cost effective manufacturing while maintaining function
frames.subject: design for cost-effective manufacturing (DFM)
frames.thread_title: Small scale manufacturing

frames.label: For comparable machines, production costs may be similar, but market demand for CNC far exceeds that for manual mills...
frames.main_point: For comparable machines, production costs may be similar, but market demand for CNC far exceeds that for manual mills; this demand difference, rather than build cost, primarily drives pricing outcomes.
frames.source_quote: The price to produce comparable CNC and manual machines might be close, but the demand for CNC's is much greater than manual machines.
frames.subject: CNC vs manual mill pricing drivers
frames.thread_title: Why are entry-level CNC mills cheaper than entry-level manual mini mills?

frames.label: In practice, most shops run overwhelmingly CNC equipment, with manual machines largely limited to tool-and-die work o...
frames.main_point: In practice, most shops run overwhelmingly CNC equipment, with manual machines largely limited to tool-and-die work or effectively retired, which concentrates demand on CNC machines.
frames.source_quote: Every shop I've ever been in, from mom & pop places to 1,000+ employees, has been 95% CNC with manual machines reserved for tool & die making or the scrap yard.
frames.subject: shop machine mix (CNC dominance)
frames.thread_title: Why are entry-level CNC mills cheaper than entry-level manual mini mills?

frames.label: CNC machines can run unattended (“lights out”), which increases their profitability relative to manual machines
frames.main_point: CNC machines can run unattended (“lights out”), which increases their profitability relative to manual machines.
frames.source_quote: the CNC machines are more profitable since they can be run lights out,
frames.subject: lights-out CNC profitability
frames.thread_title: Why are entry-level CNC mills cheaper than entry-level manual mini mills?

frames.label: Because trade schools emphasize CNC over advanced manual machining, the supply of manual machine operators is reduced
frames.main_point: Because trade schools emphasize CNC over advanced manual machining, the supply of manual machine operators is reduced.
frames.source_quote: trade schools teach focused towards CNC and less advanced skills of manual machining, so there are less manual operators available,
frames.subject: CNC-focused training reducing manual machinist supply
frames.thread_title: Why are entry-level CNC mills cheaper than entry-level manual mini mills?

frames.label: Manual mills require complex mechanical components (gears, clutches, bearings, lubrication, seals) that add significa...
frames.main_point: Manual mills require complex mechanical components (gears, clutches, bearings, lubrication, seals) that add significant cost, whereas CNC control electronics (e.g., microcontrollers) are comparatively inexpensive.
frames.source_quote: The "guts" are more complicated for manual machines, from a mechanical perspective. More gears, clutches, bearings, lubricant, seals, etc. These all cost more than a few microcontrollers to run a CNC.
frames.subject: manual mill mechanical complexity vs CNC electronics cost
frames.thread_title: Why are entry-level CNC mills cheaper than entry-level manual mini mills?

frames.label: At the low end, adding CNC capability contributes very little to total machine cost because the required electronics...
frames.main_point: At the low end, adding CNC capability contributes very little to total machine cost because the required electronics are cheap and easy to implement when high precision/quality is not the goal. This keeps entry-level CNC machines inexpensive relative to manual equivalents.
frames.source_quote: Making a machine CNC ready has a neglible cost. Electronics cost nearly nothing, and are easy to do when your not aiming to super quality.
frames.subject: entry-level CNC electronics cost impact
frames.thread_title: Why are entry-level CNC mills cheaper than entry-level manual mini mills?

frames.label: Even very cheap, lightweight CNC machines can be economically useful because a single operator can tend multiple unit...
frames.main_point: Even very cheap, lightweight CNC machines can be economically useful because a single operator can tend multiple units simultaneously. This labor leverage increases productivity despite each machine’s limited capability.
frames.source_quote: A super cheap and light CNC is actually semi useful as one operator can batch many machines.
frames.subject: operator batching across CNC machines
frames.thread_title: Why are entry-level CNC mills cheaper than entry-level manual mini mills?

frames.label: Manual milling remains constrained by one-operator-per-machine labor cost, so making the machine cheaper or lighter d...
frames.main_point: Manual milling remains constrained by one-operator-per-machine labor cost, so making the machine cheaper or lighter does not significantly improve overall economics. The operator’s time dominates the cost structure for manual machines.
frames.source_quote: Whereas a manual is still limited by the cost of a operator so it does not make sense to invest less into that use.
frames.subject: manual milling economics dominated by operator cost
frames.thread_title: Why are entry-level CNC mills cheaper than entry-level manual mini mills?

frames.label: CNC machines are better suited to production runs, while manual machines are often preferable for very small batches,...
frames.main_point: CNC machines are better suited to production runs, while manual machines are often preferable for very small batches, toolroom/modelmaking, and prototyping. Matching the tool to batch size and task type yields better effectiveness.
frames.source_quote: CNC is obviously good for production runs. But not necceserily for very small scale or toolroom, modelmaking (die) or prototype work where a manual tool is still invaluable.
frames.subject: CNC vs manual suitability by production scale and task
frames.thread_title: Why are entry-level CNC mills cheaper than entry-level manual mini mills?

frames.label: Design artifacts tend to persist longer, whereas manufacturing details need to be re-sequenced and optimized to fit c...
frames.main_point: Design artifacts tend to persist longer, whereas manufacturing details need to be re-sequenced and optimized to fit changing shop priorities. This lifecycle and scheduling difference justifies separating design documentation from manufacturing instructions.
frames.source_quote: Well the design usually has a longer time span than the manufacturing detail, and manufacturing floor might want to interleave it with different jobs at different times and optimize for different needs.
frames.subject: design vs manufacturing lifecycle and scheduling needs
frames.thread_title: Creating a drawing in Creo

frames.label: During early concept development, making quick physical mockups from simple materials (e.g., cardboard, clay, polyure...
frames.main_point: During early concept development, making quick physical mockups from simple materials (e.g., cardboard, clay, polyurethane) is an effective way to explore forms and ideas without CAD.
frames.source_quote: you can bend sheetmetals out of cardboard, you can sculpt stuff out of modeling clay, or sand out of a block of polyurethane.
frames.subject: low-fidelity physical prototyping for concept development
frames.thread_title: How did mechanical engineers work before SolidWorks?

frames.label: Do not choose non‑standard component sizes if you lack the machining capability to adapt them; odd sizes typically re...
frames.main_point: Do not choose non‑standard component sizes if you lack the machining capability to adapt them; odd sizes typically require custom machined features or mounts.
frames.source_quote: If you can't machine things then don't use oddball parts.
frames.subject: avoiding non-standard parts without machining capability
frames.thread_title: how are larger leadscrews (14mm diameter and up) fixed in place?

frames.label: High-volume processes rely on expensive dedicated machines and tooling, so their upfront cost makes small production...
frames.main_point: High-volume processes rely on expensive dedicated machines and tooling, so their upfront cost makes small production runs uneconomical even though the per-part cost is very low at scale. Low quantities cannot amortize the tooling investment.
frames.source_quote: If you need less, the initial investment into the machine and other tooling is cost prohibitive.
frames.subject: mass-production tooling amortization and low-volume economics
frames.thread_title: Making sharp tip on tube

frames.label: For low- to medium-value parts, dedicated tooling like molds, dies, or extrusion is generally only economical at volu...
frames.main_point: For low- to medium-value parts, dedicated tooling like molds, dies, or extrusion is generally only economical at volumes in the thousands; runs around a hundred are typically too small to justify the setup cost.
frames.source_quote: Unless your parts are high value, molds, dies, and extrusion machines are off the table unless you get thousands. Even a hundred might be too few.
frames.subject: volume thresholds for dedicated tooling feasibility
frames.thread_title: Making sharp tip on tube

frames.label: Continuum robots lack the rigidity needed for machining, preventing high material removal rates during roughing and m...
frames.main_point: Continuum robots lack the rigidity needed for machining, preventing high material removal rates during roughing and making it impractical to achieve tight tolerances in finishing.
frames.source_quote: It doesn't looks like these can be very rigid which means you can't hog out large amounts of material at high speed for roughing nor can you hold tight tolerances for finishing.
frames.subject: continuum robot rigidity limitations
frames.thread_title: Why continuum robots aren't common on CNC machining processes?

frames.label: Continuum-robot machining concepts face significant chip evacuation challenges, limiting their practicality for subtr...
frames.main_point: Continuum-robot machining concepts face significant chip evacuation challenges, limiting their practicality for subtractive processes in confined geometries.
frames.source_quote: On top of that are problems of chip evacuation.
frames.subject: chip evacuation in continuum-robot machining
frames.thread_title: Why continuum robots aren't common on CNC machining processes?

frames.label: A fundamental limitation for continuum robots in CNC is the lack of a reliable way to sense, locate, and calibrate th...
frames.main_point: A fundamental limitation for continuum robots in CNC is the lack of a reliable way to sense, locate, and calibrate the tool to the precision required by modern machining tolerances.
frames.source_quote: That there is no good way to sense, locate, or calibrate the tool to within acceptable tolerance limits for modern machining.
frames.subject: tool pose calibration on continuum robots
frames.thread_title: Why continuum robots aren't common on CNC machining processes?

frames.label: Cycle time dominates CNC machining economics; achieving high machining speed is critical for profitability
frames.main_point: Cycle time dominates CNC machining economics; achieving high machining speed is critical for profitability.
frames.source_quote: In CNC machining, speed is everything if you want to make money.
frames.subject: machining speed as profitability driver
frames.thread_title: Why continuum robots aren't common on CNC machining processes?

frames.label: Continuum robots’ inherent structural flexibility makes it hard for them to hold the tight positioning and machining...
frames.main_point: Continuum robots’ inherent structural flexibility makes it hard for them to hold the tight positioning and machining tolerances required in CNC work. Using them in high-precision applications risks failing to meet geometry and size specifications that rigid CNC machines routinely achieve.
frames.source_quote: Because the structure of the continuum robot is relatively flexible, it is difficult to achieve high-precision processing and positioning like a CNC machine tool.
frames.subject: precision limitations of continuum robots for CNC machining
frames.thread_title: Why continuum robots aren't common on CNC machining processes?

frames.label: Continuum robots move by deforming their entire structure, which limits their motion speed compared to traditional ri...
frames.main_point: Continuum robots move by deforming their entire structure, which limits their motion speed compared to traditional rigid/jointed robots. Consequently, they typically take longer to execute equivalent machining motions or tasks.
frames.source_quote: This is because the movement mode of the continuum robot is realized through the overall deformation, and the movement speed is slower than that of the traditional robot.
frames.subject: continuum robot motion speed vs rigid robots
frames.thread_title: Why continuum robots aren't common on CNC machining processes?

frames.label: Continuum robots usually require high-strength flexible materials and complex sensors/control, which raises their cost
frames.main_point: Continuum robots usually require high-strength flexible materials and complex sensors/control, which raises their cost.
frames.source_quote: Continuum robots usually require the use of high-strength flexible materials and complex sensor and control systems, which lead to their high cost.
frames.subject: cost drivers of continuum robots
frames.thread_title: Why continuum robots aren't common on CNC machining processes?

frames.label: CNC machines employ rigid, jointed structures with tightly controlled motion to achieve high-precision machining
frames.main_point: CNC machines employ rigid, jointed structures with tightly controlled motion to achieve high-precision machining. This architectural rigidity supports accurate positioning during operations.
frames.source_quote: CNC machine tools usually use rigid materials and joint structures during machining, and their movements are strictly controlled to achieve high-precision machining.
frames.subject: rigid jointed CNC machine architecture for precision
frames.thread_title: Why continuum robots aren't common on CNC machining processes?

frames.label: Using continuum robots for machining is problematic because their flexible structures lack the rigidity needed, causi...
frames.main_point: Using continuum robots for machining is problematic because their flexible structures lack the rigidity needed, causing instability under cutting loads and dimensional errors.
